title: Marketplace Local Launch Kit — Partner Onboarding & Tenant Entitlements
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact launch kit for partners preparing a Redwood marketplace listing that must meet local/regional requirements (data residency, trials, billing) and tenant entitlements for Dedicated/Private deployment customers. Intended audience: partner PMs, solutions engineers, and Redwood listing ops.

Scope and constraints:
- Covers EMEA, APAC (Japan, Australia), and US common divergence points.
- Focused on the minimum viable acceptance artifacts for a go-live tile + tenant entitlement mapping.
- Assumes partner has already validated legal terms with Redwood; this doc focuses on technical/ops gating and copy variants.

Quick preflight checklist (high priority, complete before intake):
- Product tile assets: 1x 1024x512 hero, 1x 512x512 icon, 3 feature screenshots (PNG, sRGB).
- Short tile copy (<= 300 chars) + long tile copy (3–4 bullet points, ~400–700 chars).
- SKU and billing mapping spreadsheet (CSV); include trial entitlement flag column.
- Security artifacts: SOC2 summary or attestation link, encryption at-rest details, KMS/HSM integration notes if Private/VPC.
- Privacy & data residency statement: where inference logs/metadata are stored, retention period, and customer opt-out options.
- Test tenant credentials for smoke tests (read-only) and contact for partner SE.

Acceptance criteria (technical):
- API compatibility: partner integration must support our standard auth header and idempotency token flow; sample curl + sample SDK snippet included in intake.
- Tenant isolation: partner must document tenant provisioning flow for Dedicated and Private (how to pass tenant_id, provisioning API endpoints, expected response codes).
- Trial provisioning: a partner-provided endpoint or mapped SKU that creates a time-limited entitlement (14 or 30 days) and returns a single-use activation token.
- Telemetry mapping: partner must provide mapping of usage events to Redwood telemetry fields (event names, token counts estimate).

Locale-specific requirements (short):
- EU (GDPR): explicit data processing addendum required; log storage in EU region for EU customers. Provide a data flow diagram or statement.
- UK: separate data residency confirmation for UK-only customers if requested.
- Japan: local language tile + screenshots; indicate support hours in JST.
- Australia: if financial vertical, confirm data residency and contract clauses for local regulators.

Tenant entitlement design pattern (recommended):
- SKU model: SKU per seat or per-compute unit. SKU metadata must include: sku_id, display_name, trial_eligible (true/false), default_quota (tokens/min).
- Entitlement lifecycle: create-entitlement -> activate (trial) -> convert-to-paid (token exchange) -> revoke. Each step should emit a webhook to Redwood tenant callback endpoint.
- Edge case: expired trial tokens should return 409 with action helpful text and link to upgrade.

Sample tile copy variants (do not copy verbatim into production; adapt tone):
- Short tile headline (bold, 60 chars): "High-throughput LLM inference for product teams"
- Short description (<=300 chars): "Run open and curated models with predictable latency across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Built-in batching, routing, and billing-ready SKUs for easy marketplace onboarding."
- Long tile bullets (~3):
  - "Production-ready inference runtime with autoscaling and failover policies for enterprise SLAs."
  - "Dedicated tenancy and private deployment options with KMS integration and audit logging."
  - "Cost-optimization toolkit: batching, caching, and quantization recommendations tailored to your workload."

SKU mapping example (CSV columns to provide):
- sku_id, sku_name, price_per_unit_usd, billing_unit, trial_days, region_restrictions, notes
- Example row: inference-basic, "Inference – Basic (per 1k tokens)", 0.12, 1000_tokens, 14, "global", "good for dev/test"

Smoke test script (ops checklist):
- Use partner test tenant and run the following: 1) authenticate via sample flow; 2) call simple generate for short prompt; 3) verify latency < 2s P50 for expected sized prompt; 4) verify tokens consumed mapped to SKU and recorded in telemetry snapshot.
- Provide logs for 3 test requests in CSV.

Operational runbook snippets (what to include in partner intake):
- Escalation contact (name, email, phone) for production incidents.
- SLO targets partner agrees to (uptime, P99 latency, error % thresholds).
- Rollback plan: partner must detail model version pinning and a fast-fallback endpoint for graceful degradation.

Localization checklist (minimum viable):
- Tile: English + partner's primary market language (JP/FR/DE).
- Screenshots: localized UI strings and captions.
- Support: indicate hours and language(s) supported.

Sample rollout timeline (8-week sprint):
- Week 0: Intake meeting, asset collection kickoff, legal checklist confirmed.
- Week 1–2: Partner provides tile assets, SKU CSV, trial endpoint, and security artifacts.
- Week 3: Redwood staging smoke tests and telemetry verification.
- Week 4: Localization pass and marketplace listing draft review.
- Week 5: Partner fixes and final legal signoff.
- Week 6: Canary enablement for a small set of customers.
- Week 7–8: Full go-live and post-launch metrics review.

Owner roles & contacts (recommended):
- Partner PM: primary contact for product decisions.
- Partner SE: integration lead for technical intake and trial endpoint.
- Redwood listing ops: intake reviewer and scheduler (email: listing-ops@redwood.ai).
- Redwood security reviewer: for SOC2 / encryption questions (sec-reviews@redwood.ai).

Unresolved questions / decisions to surface during intake:
- Trial length: 14 vs 30 days — which SKUs should be trial-eligible? (default: dev/test SKUs)
- Telemetry retention window: partner-provided logs vs Redwood retention policy—what has precedence for Private deployments?
- Model fallback semantics: should Redwood enforce a default fallback model for latency spikes or rely on partner’s multi-model endpoint?

Appendix: intake templates (copy/paste)
- Tile headline (short): ""
- Tile description (1–2 sentences): ""
- SKU CSV sample: sku_id,sku_name,price_per_unit_usd,billing_unit,trial_days,region_restrictions,notes

Notes / context:
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic and minimal — aim for fast acceptance on the marketplace while preserving legal and operational safety.
- For Private deployments, include additional network diagrams and KMS key rotation policy notes in the security artifacts bundle.
